$comment: COPY-IN BASELINE, not a live dependency — plugins do not contribute permissions, so each project owns its own deny-list. Merge these three categories into <project>/.claude/settings.json and then add whatever categories that project's blast radius requires. Permissive by design: things are denied only where no amount of agent autonomy makes them correct, never because we distrust the agent's judgment on quality.

deny: $c2: an agent that merges its own work is not a review process — review is the code-reviewer, run against the open PR by /agentic-sdlc:review

$add_your_own: Shared or blast-radius infrastructure: tofu/terraform apply and destroy, helm upgrade/install/uninstall/rollback, kubectl apply/delete/rollout, parameter-store writes. Include these whenever the project deploys into infrastructure it does not solely own. Planning and validating stays allowed — that is how a change is verified before a human applies it.
Publishing: npm/pnpm publish, if the project's packages are private.
Any path holding credentials that .env globs do not already cover.
$deliberately_allowed: Editing CI, lint, coverage and build config — the whole point is that tooling arrives incrementally and agents help build it.
Read-only and diagnostic infrastructure commands: tofu plan/validate/fmt, helm lint/template, kubectl get/describe/logs. Agents SHOULD use these.
--no-verify: moot without git hooks. If the project adds hooks, revisit.
The trade for all of the above: deliberate shortcuts get logged to docs/TOOLING-DEBT.md with an observable trigger.
